statement: On 7 Sept 2026 CM Vijay read Enforcement Directorate letters about alleged DMK-era corruption in the Assembly; the Speaker refused DMK requests to expunge them and DMK MLAs were evicted by marshals on 8 Sept. The ED material is an allegation and no court has ruled on it.

On 23 June 2026, closing the debate on the Governor's address, Vijay told a story widely read as a jibe at the Stalin family and mimicked a Stalin hand gesture; the DMK walked out and Udhayanidhi Stalin replied with personal remarks.
Around 21 Aug 2026 the Speaker expunged several allegations ruling members had made against the DMK and warned of action over reels of the expunged remarks.
Around 27 Aug 2026 the Speaker expunged remarks on jallikattu by TVK MLA M.V. Karuppaiah; the AIADMK called them derogatory and asked the CM to apologise, and no apology or TVK response was reported.
By mid-Sept 2026 Vijay had held no formal press conference as Chief Minister and spoke through scripted speeches, statements and recorded videos; ministers Rajmohan and Marie Wilson defended this.

In late June 2026 a years-old video of Minister D. Sarathkumar resurfaced which critics said showed him crushing a substance; the CM ordered an inquiry, no outcome has been published, and he remained a minister in the last report found.
response: Sarathkumar said it was a tablet being crushed for his infant daughter.

statement: In Nov 2026 Kallakurichi TVK MLA C. Arul Vignesh was accused of sending improper messages to the district Collector and visiting her home unannounced; a minister promised an inquiry once a formal complaint is filed, and a TVK disciplinary panel is to examine it.
response: Arul Vignesh denies it and calls it a DMK IT-wing campaign.

statement: On 11 Nov 2026 TVK said a party disciplinary panel would examine an allegation that Deputy Speaker M. Ravi Shankar assaulted a resident who had raised civic complaints.
response: No response from Ravi Shankar was reported; TVK referred the matter to a party disciplinary panel.

statement: In July 2026 TVK expelled a Chengalpattu functionary after a viral video allegedly showed him taking Rs 1.30 lakh from a contractor, and police arrested him the same day.
response: TVK expelled him; no statement from him was reported.

statement: On 16 Oct 2026 the DRI arrested a TVK Nagapattinam district office-bearer in a methamphetamine seizure (135 kg or 100 kg; sources differ); an NDPS case has begun with no charge sheet or court finding.
response: The TVK district secretary removed him from the party; no statement from him was reported.

statement: Two TVK functionaries were arrested in June 2026 over an alleged sexual assault, and no party action was reported.
response: No response from the accused or TVK was reported.

statement: In June 2026 YouTuber Maridhas was detained in a case Chennai cyber police registered on their own over videos critical of the CM and government; a magistrate released him on a personal bond two days later.
response: No government statement was found.

statement: An astrologer who had predicted Vijay's win was named Officer on Special Duty in the CM's office on 12 May 2026; the order was revoked the next day after allies VCK, Congress and CPI objected.

In June 2026 K. Venkata Narayana, producer of Vijay's film Jana Nayagan, was made Tamil Nadu's Special Representative in New Delhi with Cabinet rank for one year; DMK, BJP, NTK and DMDK leaders criticised it.
response: Minister K.A. Sengottaiyan called it a policy decision.

statement: The Aug 2026 budget renamed several DMK-era schemes with the prefix Vetri, for example Naan Mudhalvan became Vetri Skill Training; EPS said the government had put stickers on existing schemes, and no government response was found.
In 2021 the DMK government kept AIADMK schemes under their old names and handed out schoolbags printed with EPS's picture rather than replace them.
On 12 May 2026 TVK general secretary and Minister N. Anand told cadres not to put up banners or hoardings on roads and public places, birthdays included.
CM Vijay asked for traffic to keep moving alongside his convoy, but the convoy itself was not made smaller.
On 17 Aug 2026, after a minister referred to Karunanidhi without the customary honorific and the DMK protested, Vijay apologised to the House on the minister's behalf.
On 4 May 2021, three days before taking office, DMK cadres vandalised an Amma Canteen and Stalin had them expelled.
In 2021 the AIADMK walked out of the Assembly several times, including over the Kodanad probe; idly found no eviction or suspension of opposition MLAs in the DMK's first six months.
The DMK government said 1,21,720 campaign petitions had been received and 50,643 resolved by 29 June 2021; these are its own figures.
In May 2021 the Madras High Court ordered that the DMK's party symbol not be shown where COVID relief was handed out.
Commentator Kishore K. Swamy was arrested in June 2021 over posts about DMK leaders and detained under the Goondas Act; the High Court quashed the detention in Dec 2021 over delay.
response: The detention was quashed by the High Court on grounds of delay; no DMK government response is given in idly's report.

statement: Stalin asked for an end to public receptions and banners for ministers in 2021 (date not confirmed).
On 17 Aug 2016 DMK MLAs were evicted and suspended for a week on a ruling-party resolution, and the High Court declined to stay the suspension; sources differ on whether 79 or 89 MLAs were suspended.
After CM Jayalalithaa entered hospital on 22 Sept 2016, only the hospital issued health updates, with no government statement by 22 Oct.

In 2016 police booked people over social-media rumours about the CM's health; counts differ by date and outlet (43 cases per DT Next, at least 8 arrests per TNM), and the NHRC chairman said arrest may not be the answer.
Hearing a case in Aug 2016, the Supreme Court told the Tamil Nadu government it must face criticism and not use criminal defamation against opponents.
In Aug 2016 Dairy Minister S.P. Shanmuganathan was dropped with no reason given, and MP Sasikala Pushpa was expelled from the AIADMK.
The state's own list shows 213 criminal defamation cases against opponents and media from May 2011 to July 2016, not broken down by year.
Police fired on protesters at Paramakudi on 11 Sept 2011; six or seven people died (sources differ).
response: CM Jayalalithaa said the police fired in self-defence.

statement: A retired judge was appointed to inquire into the 2011 Paramakudi firing on Dalit protesters.
In 2011 the Law Minister was removed on 3 July with no reason given, and six ministers were dropped on 4 Nov; the reasons came from news reports, not official statements.
A 2017 retrospective described the 2011-16 AIADMK government as one that hardly ever spoke to the media; it covers the whole term, not just the first six months.
In 2011 a Sun Pictures executive was arrested on distributors' complaints.
response: No response from the accused side is recorded in idly's report.

statement: TNM counted a death in Thoothukudi in July 2026 as the fourth alleged custodial death since May; a magistrate's inquiry was ordered.
response: Police deny assault.

statement: In June 2021 a man died after a police beating in Salem, and the officer was removed and charged with murder.
In Sept 2016 a murder accused died in Puzhal prison, and his lawyer disputed the official account.

In each change of government idly examined (2011, 2021, 2026), police or the vigilance department moved against leaders of the outgoing party within months; each time the outgoing party called it vendetta and the new government said it was following complaints or court orders.
The AIADMK government set up police land-grab cells in July 2011, and by 17 Aug it reported 8,947 complaints and 419 arrests (government figures).
response: Karunanidhi said government action was going beyond limits and Stalin called them false cases.

statement: Former DMK minister Veerapandi S. Arumugam was arrested on 30 July 2011 in a land-grab case; there was no conviction in the window, and in 2012 the High Court quashed his Goondas Act detention.
response: Stalin called them false cases and the DMK protested statewide on 1 Aug 2011.

statement: Former DMK minister K.N. Nehru was arrested on 25 Aug 2011 in a land-grab case; there was no conviction in the window.
response: The DMK called the land-grab cases false and politically motivated.

statement: Chepauk MLA J. Anbazhagan (arrested 30 July 2011) and former DMK minister N.K.K.P. Raja were among DMK leaders arrested in the 2011 land-grab drive; there was no conviction in the window.
response: The DMK called them false cases.

statement: In July 2011 the police officer heading the land-grab cell said there were no political overtones to its actions.
In July 2021 the DVAC searched 21 properties linked to former AIADMK minister M.R. Vijayabhaskar; these are allegations with no conviction in the window.
response: The AIADMK accused the DMK of vengeance and said it was hiding its failures behind raids.

statement: On 10 Aug 2021 the DVAC searched about 52 premises of former AIADMK minister S.P. Velumani on an FIR alleging favouritism in corporation tenders, filed after a High Court direction; no conviction in the window.
response: The AIADMK accused the DMK of vengeance and of hiding its failures behind raids.

statement: On 16 Sept 2021 the DVAC searched 28 places linked to former AIADMK minister K.C. Veeramani over alleged disproportionate assets of Rs 28 crore; no conviction in the window.
response: The AIADMK accused the DMK of vengeance and of hiding its failures behind raids.

statement: In Aug 2021 Stalin told the Assembly that action against former AIADMK ministers followed court directions and was not vendetta.

DMK MLA Anitha R. Radhakrishnan was arrested on 3 July 2026 over a speech against the CM, on a TVK functionary's complaint, after the High Court refused anticipatory bail and asked why an MLA should use such language.
response: Kanimozhi and the DMK called the arrests of DMK legislators political vendetta.

statement: DMK MLA G.V. Markandayan was arrested on 20 July 2026 over a 'break your bones' remark against CM Vijay, on a TVK functionary's complaint, and the High Court granted him bail on 3 Aug.
response: The DMK called it political vendetta; Law Minister Nirmal Kumar said Markandayan spoke in a threatening manner.

statement: Udhayanidhi Stalin was arrested on 4 Aug 2026 over a double-meaning remark, on a TVK functionary's complaint, and released the same day after the state told the High Court police only wanted to question him.
response: The DMK called it political vendetta; EPS condemned the remark but called the arrest on the eve of the session unwarranted. TVK called the case a warning to those who speak ill of women.

statement: Former DMK minister K.N. Nehru was searched on 5 Sept 2026 and questioned around 29 Oct in an alleged Rs 634 crore recruitment bribery case; he was not arrested and the High Court has stayed further vigilance action.
response: Stalin called the raids 'Vettri Vendetta Politics'.

statement: Greater Chennai Police CCB is investigating former DMK School Education Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi under the Prevention of Corruption Act over money allegedly collected from private school managements as a 'party fund' for promised approvals; the complaint was reported as over Rs 100 crore and police told the court they had traced Rs 17,26,73,650.
response: In Sept 2026 Anbil Mahesh called the searches politically motivated and said nothing illegal was found; Stalin called it political vendetta.

statement: On 26 Oct 2026 the Madras High Court refused Anbil Mahesh anticipatory bail, saying custodial interrogation was warranted, and he was arrested that evening; DT Next called him the first former minister arrested for graft under the TVK government.
response: Stalin called the case political vendetta and said Anbil Mahesh would face it legally.

statement: A Special Court sent Anbil Mahesh to judicial custody on 27 Oct 2026, granted three days of police custody on 30 Oct and extended custody to 18 Nov on 6 Nov.
response: In Sept 2026 Anbil Mahesh called the searches politically motivated and said nothing illegal was found; Stalin called the case political vendetta.

statement: On 10 Nov 2026 the Special Court refused Anbil Mahesh bail, saying the material showed a prima facie economic offence and the probe was at an early stage; no charge sheet has been reported.
response: On 5 Nov his lawyers argued the alleged bribe-givers had not been arrested, a collective government decision was being painted as corruption, and the Governor's sanction to prosecute had not been obtained; no response to the 10 Nov order was reported.

statement: A CBI case on alleged irregularities in TANGEDCO transformer tenders worth Rs 397 crore followed a High Court order made before TVK took office.
response: Former minister Senthil Balaji denies any loss.

statement: The TVK government ordered government jobs for relatives of those who died in the 27 Sept 2025 Karur crowd crush and handed over 32 appointment orders; the Madras High Court quashed the order on 27 July 2026 and the Supreme Court stayed that ruling on 14 Aug 2026.

On 7 July 2026 the Supreme Court declined a DMK plea to stop the CM and others speaking about the Karur case or meeting victims' families, noted the CM is not an accused in the FIRs, and said 'You counter their speech with your speech'; the DMK withdrew.

On 13 Oct 2025, on TVK's petition, the Supreme Court moved the Karur probe from a High Court-appointed police team to the CBI under a committee led by former judge Ajay Rastogi, and paused the state's one-member inquiry.
On 23 Oct 2025 the CBI filed a first inquiry report on Karur in the Karur magistrate's court; it was not a charge sheet.
On 2 Dec 2025 the then DMK government asked the Supreme Court to cancel the CBI probe into Karur and restore the police team, saying the police probe was conducted in a fair and unbiased manner.
TVK's first cabinet has 7 SC (Dalit) ministers, or 8 counting VCK's Vanni Arasu, as reported by outlets; no government publishes ministers' caste.
The DMK's 2021 cabinet had 3 SC ministers at formation and 4 from Sept 2024, as reported.
The AIADMK's 2016 first cabinet had 2 or 3 SC ministers (sources differ).
TVK's first cabinet has 4 women ministers.
The DMK's 2021 first cabinet had 2 women ministers.
The AIADMK's 2016 first cabinet had 3 or 4 women ministers, depending on whether the CM is counted.
The AIADMK's 2011 first cabinet had 2 or 3 women ministers (sources differ).
TVK's cabinet has 2 Muslim ministers, including IUML's A.M. Shahjahan.
The DMK's 2021 first cabinet had 2 Muslim ministers.
In Oct 2025 the DMK government announced a commission under retired judge K.N. Basha to draft an honour-killing law.
In May 2026, after the VCK raised it in the Assembly, DT Next reported that the honour-killing panel lacked computers and phones and had not started work.
Justice K.N. Basha said his commission's office was set up only in April 2026, its term was extended to May 2027, and police recorded only 13 honour-killing cases between 2014 and 2026.
On 6 July 2026 Social Justice Minister Vanni Arasu said the government was determined to enact a separate law against honour killings; no bill had been introduced by 10 Nov 2026.
On 18 Oct 2026 the honour-killing commission said TVK, DMK, AIADMK and PMK had not sent their views a month after being asked, while Congress, VCK, both Communist parties, IUML and MMK had.
In the Governor's address of 18 June 2026 the TVK government said it would run a Social Justice Survey after the Union completes its caste count, and pledged to protect 69% reservation.
On 29 Oct 2026 the Cabinet approved a commission under a retired judge to draft guidelines for the Social Justice Survey, to roll out next year.
PMK founder S. Ramadoss asked CM Vijay for a Vanniyar quota based on caste data; no decision on it was found.
On 19 June 2026 the HR&CE department cancelled DMK-era approvals for 46 temple-fund projects worth Rs 246 crore, none started, citing temple finances; Hindu Munnani and BJP figures welcomed it.
The TVK budget announced a five-year mission to renovate 3,000 temples.
In May 2026, after complaints that both the HR&CE minister and secretary came from one 'upper caste' community, the secretary was moved.
response: Minister S. Ramesh denied that his posting was based on caste.

statement: On 27 Aug 2026 Minorities Welfare Minister A.M. Shahjahan (IUML) announced full tuition for Muslim women in government-quota undergraduate seats, a Waqf women's college and a Rs 100 crore interest-free fund for Waqf and Christian properties.
The TVK budget raised the Haj subsidy for first-time pilgrims from Rs 25,000 to Rs 35,000.
The Adi Dravidar and Tribal Welfare Department was renamed the Social Justice Department.
response: Minister Vanni Arasu said funds would not be diverted.

statement: On 25 June 2026 the Madras High Court quashed a 2024 DMK order letting converts to Islam from backward and SC groups get backward-class Muslim certificates; the TVK government appealed on 8 July and by 15 Oct the Supreme Court had upheld the High Court.
In Sept 2021 the DMK government brought a bill for a state SC/ST Commission; idly's only source for this is a DMK party publication.
Vijay attended the NITI Aayog Governing Council on 11 June 2026; Stalin had skipped it in some years.
On 18 June 2026 the Governor read the government's address in full, the first uninterrupted address in three years.
On 11 Oct 2026 PM Modi and Vijay opened a Chennai Metro stretch and rode it together; Modi said he would work with the state despite the change of government.
Analysts quoted by ThePrint after Vijay's first Delhi visit as CM called his tone toward the Centre assertive but not hostile.
The TVK government opposes NEP 2020 and NEET, keeps the two-language policy, wants education moved to the State List and admissions based on Class 12 marks.
The TVK government opposes Karnataka's Mekedatu dam without Tamil Nadu's consent and seeks the release of fishermen held by Sri Lanka, raised with PM Modi in May 2026.
In the June 2026 Governor's address the government promised an Assembly resolution on fair devolution and a legal committee to pursue it up to the Supreme Court.
Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar held additional charge as Tamil Nadu Governor from March 2026 and was made full-time Governor on 12 Oct 2026.
Of the 13 bills passed in the TVK government's first session, Governor Arlekar signed 12 and sent one, cutting the land minimum for private universities, to the President, with no reason reported.
In April 2025 the Supreme Court held that Governor R.N. Ravi's reserving of 10 re-passed bills for the President was illegal.

A government order of 6 Nov 2026 wound up the Union-state relations committee under former Supreme Court judge Kurian Joseph, set up by the DMK in April 2025, as redundant, saying its work overlaps with the State Law Commission.
Stalin said scrapping the Kurian Joseph committee lost a chance to strengthen federalism; the CPI and Dravidar Kazhagam opposed the move and the BJP welcomed it.
Finishing the Kurian Joseph committee's report was one of the VCK's conditions for supporting the TVK government in May 2026.

The amount Tamil Nadu says the Centre owes it under Samagra Shiksha has changed with each statement: Rs 3,284 crore on 11 June, Rs 3,458 crore on 18 June and Rs 5,110 crore on 11 Oct 2026; no source reconciles them.

On 14 June 2026 Stalin asked whether Vijay had gone to Delhi to escape the Karur CBI case and whether he was afraid to criticise the BJP; on 18 June Udhayanidhi said the Governor reading every line fed suspicion of a tacit understanding with the BJP.
response: No direct TVK reply is recorded in idly's report; idly found no document, agreement or on-record statement showing such an understanding.

statement: Vijay has not been reported attacking the BJP by name as CM.

TVK governs with two Congress ministers, and in early Oct 2026 TVK ministers attended a Tamil Nadu INDIA bloc meeting for the first time and called it a formal declaration of TVK being part of the alliance.
The state BJP chief has attacked the TVK government, warning it against 'DMK-style' corruption.

In its first six months the DMK government in 2021 passed Assembly resolutions against the farm laws and the CAA and a NEET exemption bill; TVK passed no resolution of that kind in its first six months that idly found.
In 2011 Jayalalithaa's cabinet asked the Centre to halt work at Kudankulam, and she blamed the Centre's 'step-motherly treatment' when raising bus fares and milk prices in Nov 2011.
Sun News and Dinakaran are owned by Kalanithi Maran's Sun Group; the Maran family is related to the Karunanidhi (DMK) family, and the outlets are widely seen as pro-DMK (TNM 2014/15; Scroll 2020).

Kalaignar TV / Seithigal is owned by the Karunanidhi family, including DMK MP Kanimozhi, and was launched as DMK-backed; TNM (2014/15) called it the DMK's mouthpiece. Current shareholding is unverified.

Jaya TV is owned by the Sasikala family; it was AIADMK-linked until 2017 and since then sits with the Sasikala and T.T.V. Dhinakaran camp; TNM (2014/15) called it openly pro-AIADMK. Current shareholding is unverified.
News J (Mantaro Network) was launched by the AIADMK in 2018; it says it is not a party mouthpiece.

Puthiya Thalaimurai is owned by the SRM group (Pachamuthu family), whose party IJK joined the AIADMK-NDA side in March 2026 after earlier alliances with the DMK (2019) and BJP (2024); TNM (2014/15) saw no obvious lean.
The Federal shares an owner with Puthiya Thalaimurai and so the same IJK link; idly marks facts resting on it alone as one source.

Thanthi TV and DT Next belong to the Daily Thanthi group (Adityan family) with no documented party link; TNM (2014/15) called it largely free of bias and S. Arasu (2021) called the parent daily pro-establishment. Current shareholding is unverified.
News18 Tamil Nadu is owned by Network18 (about 75% Reliance) with no documented party link; a 2020 online campaign accused it of DMK bias, which Network18 denied (Scroll 2020).
Polimer News is owned by the P.V. Kalyanasundaram family; its founder is a former DMK leader and no current party link is documented.
Dinamalar is owned by the R. Lakshmipathy family with no documented party link and says it is not aligned; S. Arasu (2021) described it as the daily most favourable to the BJP.
Dinamani and The New Indian Express are owned by Express Publications (Madurai), Manoj Sonthalia, with no documented party link.
Vikatan is owned by the Vasan family with no documented party link; its website was blocked by the Union government in 2025 over a cartoon of the PM and the High Court ordered it unblocked.
The Hindu is owned by the Kasturi family with no documented party link.
The News Minute is owned by Spunklane Media, part-owned by Quint Digital, with no documented party link.
South First is Hyderabad-based with undisclosed investors and no documented party link; it calls itself non-partisan.
Smaller channels have documented party links: Captain TV (DMDK), Makkal TV (PMK), Velicham TV (VCK, a TVK ally), and Mega TV and Vasanth TV (Congress leaders; Congress is also a TVK ally).
TVK has no documented outlet of its own; trade press described a channel called Vettri News as TVK's proposed mouthpiece, but TVK did not announce it.

Tamil Nadu budget head 2220 (Information and Publicity) was Rs 243.53 crore in the 2026-27 interim budget and Rs 278.91 crore revised; the head covers memorials, journalists' welfare, accreditation and digital content, and no source splits out advertising.

The 2023-24 policy note shows publicity spending of Rs 104.33 crore in 2021-22 (digit grouping uncertain), Rs 145.11 crore revised for 2022-23 and Rs 139.01 crore budgeted for 2023-24; these are not comparable line for line with 2026-27.

sources.outlet: Tamil Nadu Information and Publicity policy note 2023-24

statement: On 2 June 2026 the TVK government was reported to be considering cutting advertisement spending and moving tender and land notices online; the revised 2026-27 publicity figure is still higher than the interim one.

On 16 May 2012 the AIADMK government ran first-anniversary jacket advertisements in national dailies, costed at Rs 25 crore by Firstpost and NDTV; the same report put the earlier DMK government's 2009-11 anniversary advertising for Rajiv and Indira Gandhi at about Rs 30 crore. Neither figure is official.

A South First reporter posing as a client found some pro-Vijay reels were paid, at Rs 20,000 to Rs 75,000 a video per screenshots; the outlet could not establish who paid and said not all pro-Vijay content is paid.
response: A TVK national spokesperson said: 'There is absolutely no need for us to pay for PR.'

statement: On 22 Apr 2026 two Chennai residents asked the state's Chief Electoral Officer to act on an alleged planned TVK online campaign during the silent period, including bot networks; no outcome was reported.
response: No TVK response was reported.

statement: In Oct 2026 DMK IT wing secretary T.R.B. Rajaa and MP Kanimozhi alleged that Instagram posts critical of the TVK government were being taken down through misuse of reporting tools, and Kanimozhi asked the Union IT Minister whether police were involved.
response: No response from the state government or Meta was reported.

statement: On 28 Oct 2026 Chennai police in plain clothes picked up an academic at 5 am over an abusive Instagram comment about a TVK MLA that had been posted from a fake account using his photo; he was released by about 7:45 am.
response: Law Minister C.T.R. Nirmal Kumar called it a mistake that had been put right; Stalin called it the 'peak of fascism'.

statement: In Apr 2025 Greater Chennai Police sent X two notices to remove 18 posts critical of Stalin, Udhayanidhi Stalin and the DMK government and asked for account details; this came out in X's lawsuit in the Karnataka High Court.

No court, Election Commission or platform finding against any Tamil Nadu party on fake accounts or paid influencers was found; Meta's April 2019 takedown of coordinated networks in India named a Congress IT Cell network but no Tamil Nadu party.

idly's digest is a reading of 5,512 YouTube comments from 4,975 accounts under 90 videos, mostly from Tamil news channels, posted 10 May-10 Nov 2026 (3,306 Tamil, 2,089 English, 117 Latin-script Tamil); it is not a poll, Reddit and X were not read, and three channels (NewsTamil 24X7, Puthiyathalaimurai, Thanthi TV) hold more than a quarter of the comments.

In idly's reading of 5,512 YouTube comments (not a poll; themes matched by keyword, most comments matched none), the most-discussed themes by distinct commenters were welfare schemes (303), state debt (202), votes and cash for votes (173), corruption (163), Rs 2,500 and other cash promises (161) and jobs (147); few touched arrests of opponents (28) or caste and religion (19).

In idly's reading of 5,512 YouTube comments (not a poll), TVK or Vijay were named by 919 people, the DMK or Stalin by 407, the NTK or Seeman by 108, the AIADMK or Palaniswami by 89, the BJP and Centre by 30 and the Congress by 23; the videos come from channels with their own leans.

In idly's reading of 5,512 YouTube comments (not a poll; tone is a crude word match and praise is inflated by fan activity), praise words outnumbered criticism words in comments naming only TVK in every month from May to Oct 2026, and in 1-10 Nov criticism edged ahead 8 to 7; the November numbers are too small to be a finding.

No scientific opinion poll of the TVK government was found; South First spoke to just over 100 people on 8-9 Nov 2026 in an informal survey with no stated sampling method, in which most answers were negative, and idly does not report its percentages because it is not a poll.
